scenario: 口头描述 YouTube 的「召回→排序→重排」流程要花 2-3 分钟，面试官还容易跟丢。
scenario_en: Verbally describing YouTube's candidate-generation to ranking to re-ranking flow costs 2-3 minutes and the interviewer can lose the thread.
q: 在 ML SD 面试里画图的核心价值是什么？
q_en: What is the core value of diagramming in an ML SD interview?
why: 一张好图把口头讲要 2-3 分钟的流程瞬间说清，省下的分钟可以投到取舍推理上。图是把「解释」压缩成「指认」的杠杆，不是装饰。
why_en: A good diagram makes instantly legible what verbal explanation costs 2-3 minutes, buying those minutes back for tradeoff reasoning.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["澄清后
高层系统图"] --> D["数据策略
数据流图"] D --> M["模型设计
架构草图(非平凡才画)"]
options: 让白板看起来更专业、更有仪表感
把口头要 2-3 分钟的流程瞬间说清，省下的分钟投到取舍推理上
证明你会用画图软件，展示工具熟练度
把设计画得越复杂越好，用细节量压住面试官
options_en: Make the whiteboard look more professional and polished.
Make instantly legible what verbal explanation costs 2-3 min, buying minutes back for tradeoff reasoning.
Prove you can use diagramming software and show tool proficiency.
Draw the design as complex as possible to overwhelm the interviewer with detail.
optionExplanations: 仪表感不是目的；图的价值在省时间和防跟丢，不在好看。
对；图＝把解释压成指认的杠杆，省下的 2-3 分钟正好投到取舍深挖。
面试不评你的画图软件熟练度，评的是设计沟通效率。
越复杂越好正好相反——过度工程是本课点名的常见错误。
optionExplanations_en: Polish is not the point; a diagram's value is saving time and preventing lost threads, not looks.
Correct — a diagram is a lever compressing explanation into pointing, and the 2-3 min saved goes into deeper tradeoffs.
The interview does not score software proficiency; it scores design-communication efficiency.
As-complex-as-possible is the opposite; over-engineering is a common mistake this lesson names.

scenario: 整场面试你可能画三种不同用途的图，各自对应框架的不同阶段。
scenario_en: Across the interview you may draw three purpose-specific diagram types, each mapping to a different framework phase.
q: ML SD 面试的三种核心图是哪三种？
q_en: What are the three core diagram types in an ML SD interview?
why: 三种：高层系统图（组件+箭头，澄清后画）、数据流图（原始→训练→预测→反馈，数据策略时画）、模型架构草图（内部结构，模型设计且非平凡时画）。各对应框架的一个阶段。
why_en: The three are the high-level system diagram, the data-flow diagram, and the model-architecture sketch, each mapping to a framework phase.
options: 类图、时序图、状态机图（这是软件工程通用三件套，不是本课的三种）
高层系统图、数据流图、模型架构草图
折线图、柱状图、饼图（这是数据可视化图表，不是系统设计图）
甘特图、燃尽图、看板（这是项目管理图，不是 ML 设计图）
options_en: Class, sequence, and state diagrams (the generic software-engineering trio, not this lesson's three).
High-level system diagram, data-flow diagram, and model-architecture sketch.
Line, bar, and pie charts (data-visualization charts, not system-design diagrams).
Gantt, burndown, and kanban (project-management charts, not ML design diagrams).
optionExplanations: 类图/时序图是通用 SWE 图，不是 ML SD 面试专用的这三种。
对；高层系统图/数据流图/模型架构草图，分别服务澄清、数据、模型三个阶段。
折线/柱/饼是数据图表，用来展示数据分布，不是设计系统结构。
甘特/燃尽/看板是项目管理工具，和设计一个 ML 系统的结构无关。
optionExplanations_en: Class and sequence diagrams are generic SWE diagrams, not the three specific to ML SD interviews.
Correct — high-level system, data-flow, and model-architecture sketch serve the clarify, data, and model phases.
Line/bar/pie are data charts for showing distributions, not for designing system structure.
Gantt/burndown/kanban are project-management tools, unrelated to structuring an ML system.

scenario: 问题澄清刚做完（约第 5-8 分钟），你要给整场设计立一个共享的心智模型。
scenario_en: Clarification just finished (around min 5-8) and you want to anchor a shared mental model for the whole design.
q: 高层系统图该什么时候画，能不能跳过？
q_en: When should the high-level system diagram be drawn, and can it be skipped?
why: 高层系统图要在澄清之后尽早画（约 min 5-8），因为它给双方立一个共享心智模型，后面所有讨论都挂在它上面。它是唯一「永不跳过」的图。
why_en: Draw the high-level system diagram early right after clarification (about min 5-8), because it anchors a shared mental model, and it is the one diagram you never skip.
whenOtherWins: 没有反例——高层系统图始终要画；若系统极简（单模型无外围组件），可以画得很小，但仍要画。
options: 等讲完所有细节后，在最后 5 分钟补一张总览图
澄清之后尽早画（约 min 5-8），它立起共享心智模型，且永不跳过
只在面试官明确要求时才画，否则省时间不画
在模型设计阶段画，因为那时才知道有哪些组件
options_en: Draw a summary diagram in the last 5 minutes after all details are done.
Draw it early right after clarification (about min 5-8); it anchors a shared mental model and is never skipped.
Only draw it if the interviewer explicitly asks, otherwise skip to save time.
Draw it during model design, since only then do you know the components.
optionExplanations: 最后补图时心智模型早已（错误地）成型，事后画没有价值——这是「画太晚」的错误。
对；澄清后尽早画立共享心智模型，是三种图里唯一永不跳过的。
等面试官要求才画就晚了，高层图是你主动立框架的工具，不该被动等。
组件在澄清后就大致清楚了，等到模型设计才画会错过锚定讨论的最佳时机。
optionExplanations_en: A late diagram comes after the mental model already (mis)formed and adds no value — the 'too late' mistake.
Correct — drawing it early after clarification anchors a shared model and is the only never-skip diagram of the three.
Waiting to be asked is too late; the high-level diagram is your proactive framing tool, not something to wait on.
Components are roughly clear after clarification; waiting until model design misses the best moment to anchor the discussion.

scenario: 数据策略阶段（约 min 8-15），你在讲数据从原始日志一路到训练、预测、再回流重训。
scenario_en: During data strategy (about min 8-15) you are explaining data from raw logs through training, prediction, and back to retraining.
q: 数据流图该在哪一步画？什么情况可以跳过？
q_en: At which step is the data-flow diagram drawn, and when can it be skipped?
why: 数据流图在数据策略阶段画（约 min 8-15），追踪原始数据→训练数据→预测→反馈回流。若管线本身很平凡（单一静态数据集、无反馈），可以跳过——画了也没增量。
why_en: Draw the data-flow diagram during data strategy (about min 8-15) to trace raw to training to predictions to the feedback loop, and skip it when the pipeline is trivial.
whenOtherWins: 若数据管线是单一静态数据集、没有反馈回流，就跳过数据流图，把时间留给别处。
options: 问题澄清阶段画，越早越好，和数据无关
数据策略阶段画（约 min 8-15）；若管线平凡（单一静态数据集、无反馈）可跳过
监控阶段画，因为反馈回流属于监控
任何阶段都必须画，数据流图和高层图一样永不跳过
options_en: Draw it in the clarification phase, the earlier the better, unrelated to data.
Draw it during data strategy (about min 8-15); skip if the pipeline is trivial (single static dataset, no feedback).
Draw it during monitoring, since the feedback loop belongs to monitoring.
Always draw it; the data-flow diagram, like the high-level one, is never skipped.
optionExplanations: 澄清阶段还没进入数据讨论，画数据流图时机不对。
对；数据流图配合数据策略讲管线，平凡管线（静态数据集无反馈）没必要画。
反馈回流是数据流图的一部分，但整张图在数据策略阶段就该画，不是等到监控。
数据流图是可跳过的（管线平凡时），只有高层系统图才永不跳过。
optionExplanations_en: Clarification has not entered the data discussion yet, so drawing a data-flow diagram there is mistimed.
Correct — the data-flow diagram accompanies the data-strategy pipeline talk, and a trivial pipeline (static dataset, no feedback) need not be drawn.
The feedback loop is part of the data-flow diagram, but the whole diagram belongs in data strategy, not monitoring.
The data-flow diagram is skippable when the pipeline is trivial; only the high-level system diagram is never skipped.

scenario: 模型设计阶段（约 min 15-22），你要决定要不要画一张模型内部结构草图。
scenario_en: In model design (about min 15-22) you must decide whether to sketch the model's internal structure.
q: 模型架构草图什么时候该画、什么时候该跳过？
q_en: When should you draw the model-architecture sketch, and when skip it?
why: 只在架构非平凡时画（双塔检索、多任务），画输入特征、层类型、embedding 维度、输出头、损失。若模型一句话说得清（逻辑回归、XGBoost），画草图就是浪费时间，直接口头说。
why_en: Sketch it only when the architecture is non-trivial (two-tower, multi-task), and skip it when the model is one-sentence describable like logistic regression or XGBoost.
whenOtherWins: 架构非平凡（双塔、多任务、多输出头、特殊交互层）时才值得画草图，标清输入维度、层类型、损失函数。
options: 任何模型都画草图，越详细越能显示深度
只在架构非平凡时画（双塔、多任务）；一句话能说清的模型（逻辑回归、XGBoost）跳过
只画一句话能说清的简单模型，复杂模型太难画就口头带过
在澄清阶段就画好，免得后面没时间
options_en: Sketch every model — the more detailed the more depth it shows.
Sketch only when the architecture is non-trivial (two-tower, multi-task); skip one-sentence models (logistic regression, XGBoost).
Only sketch simple one-sentence models; complex models are too hard to draw, so just describe them verbally.
Draw it during clarification so you do not run out of time later.
optionExplanations: 任何模型都画会在简单模型上浪费时间——一句话能说清的模型画草图没增量。
对；草图只为「空间关系重要」的非平凡架构服务，简单模型口头说更省时。
说反了：该画的恰恰是复杂架构（空间关系重要），简单模型才跳过。
澄清阶段还没定模型，画草图时机不对，应在模型设计阶段画。
optionExplanations_en: Sketching every model wastes time on simple ones — a one-sentence model gains nothing from a sketch.
Correct — the sketch serves only non-trivial architectures where spatial relationships matter; describe simple models verbally.
Reversed: the ones worth sketching are complex architectures (spatial relationships matter); simple models are what you skip.
Clarification has not fixed the model yet, so a sketch there is mistimed; draw it in model design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络末端针对某个任务的输出层；多任务模型有多个头。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An output head is the task-specific output layer at the end of a network; multi-task models have several.

scenario: 你画了高层系统图，但箭头都没写字，面试官盯着一条箭头问「这条代表什么？」
scenario_en: You drew a high-level system diagram but left arrows unlabeled, and the interviewer asks 'what does this arrow represent?'
q: 最常见的画图错误是什么，代价多大？
q_en: What is the single most common diagramming mistake, and what does it cost?
why: 未标注的箭头是最常见的画图错误：每条都逼面试官打断问「这代表什么」，一次约 15-20 秒。修法是每条箭头都标清流的是什么（「搜索请求」「特征向量」「排序结果」）。
why_en: Unlabeled arrows are the most common mistake, each forcing a 15-20 second interrupt asking what it represents, fixed by labeling every arrow with what flows.
options: 颜色用得太少，图看起来单调
未标注的箭头：每条逼面试官打断问「这代表什么」，一次约 15-20 秒
框画得不够方正，影响美观
图画在白板左边而不是正中间
options_en: Using too few colors, making the diagram look dull.
Unlabeled arrows: each forces the interviewer to interrupt asking what it represents, about 15-20 sec each.
Boxes not drawn squarely enough, hurting aesthetics.
Drawing on the left of the whiteboard instead of dead center.
optionExplanations: 颜色单调不影响理解，不是评分或效率问题。
对；未标箭头是头号错误，每条制造一次 15-20 秒打断，标清流的是什么即可消除。
框正不正方不影响理解，不是本课点名的错误。
画在哪一侧无关紧要，不构成沟通障碍。
optionExplanations_en: Dull colors do not impede understanding and are neither a scoring nor an efficiency issue.
Correct — unlabeled arrows are the number-one mistake, each causing a 15-20 sec interrupt, removed by labeling what flows.
Whether boxes are square does not impede understanding and is not a mistake this lesson names.
Which side you draw on is irrelevant and creates no communication barrier.

scenario: 画图时要有一套统一的标注纪律，让每张图自解释。
scenario_en: You need consistent labeling discipline so every diagram is self-explanatory.
q: 画图的标注纪律具体包含什么？
q_en: What does diagram labeling discipline specifically include?
why: 纪律：每个框都命名、每条箭头都标注流的是什么，并在关键处加量化注解——serving 箭头上标 QPS、ETL 上标批处理频率、草图里标 embedding 维度。量化注解证明你在想扩展、延迟、漂移。
why_en: Name every box, label every arrow with what flows, and add quantitative annotations where they matter, like QPS on serving, batch frequency in ETL, and embedding dims in the sketch.
options: 只给最重要的两三个框命名，其余留白保持简洁
每个框命名、每条箭头标流的是什么，并在关键处加量化注解（QPS、批频率、embedding 维度）
把所有超参数和层数都写进图里，越全越好
只标箭头不标框，框的含义靠口头补充
options_en: Name only the two or three most important boxes and leave the rest blank for simplicity.
Name every box, label every arrow with what flows, and add quantitative annotations where they matter (QPS, batch frequency, embedding dims).
Write every hyperparameter and layer count into the diagram — the more complete the better.
Label arrows only, not boxes; convey box meaning verbally.
optionExplanations: 只命名部分框会留下无名框，制造「这是什么」的打断，纪律要求每个框都命名。
对；框命名+箭头标注+关键处量化注解，让图自解释，还顺带秀出你在想扩展/延迟/漂移。
把超参层数全塞进图是过度细节，图要停在组件层，不是塞满参数。
只标箭头不标框会留无名框，靠口头补充等于放弃图的自解释性。
optionExplanations_en: Naming only some boxes leaves nameless ones that trigger 'what is this' interrupts; discipline requires naming every box.
Correct — name boxes, label arrows, and add quantitative annotations where they matter, making the diagram self-explanatory and signaling scaling/latency/drift awareness.
Cramming every hyperparameter is over-detail; a diagram stays at the component level, not stuffed with parameters.
Labeling arrows only leaves nameless boxes, and verbal patching abandons the diagram's self-explanatory value.

scenario: 画图有几类常见错误会拖累而非帮助沟通，要能一一识别。
scenario_en: Several classes of diagramming mistakes hurt rather than help communication and must be recognized.
q: 以下哪些是本课点名的常见画图错误？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are the common diagramming mistakes named in this lesson? (multiple)
why: 常见错误：过度工程（画 K8s pods、负载均衡、DB 分片这些 DevOps 细节）、画太晚（先口头 20 分钟才补图）、组件无标注、从不更新（设计演进了图却停在旧版，会主动误导）。
why_en: Common mistakes are over-engineering with DevOps detail, drawing too late, unlabeled components, and never updating a stale diagram.
options: 过度工程：画 K8s pods、负载均衡、DB 分片等 DevOps 细节
画太晚：先口头讲 20 分钟，最后才补一张事后诸葛的图
组件无标注 / 从不更新：设计演进了图却停在旧版，主动误导
用了箭头连接组件（这是正常画法，不是错误）
options_en: Over-engineering: drawing K8s pods, load balancers, DB sharding and other DevOps detail.
Drawing too late: 20 minutes of verbal first, then an afterthought diagram.
Unlabeled components / never updating: the design evolves but the diagram stays stale and misleads.
Using arrows to connect components (this is normal practice, not a mistake).
optionExplanations: 对；画 DevOps 细节是过度工程，面试评 ML 判断不是运维，除非被问否则停在组件层。
对；先口头 20 分钟再补图，心智模型早已成型，事后图没价值。
对；无标注制造打断，从不更新的旧图会主动误导，两者都是常见错误。
用箭头连组件是正常画法本身，不是错误——错误是箭头没标注。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — DevOps detail is over-engineering; the interview scores ML judgment not ops, so stay at component level unless asked.
Correct — 20 minutes of verbal then a late diagram comes after the mental model formed, so it adds no value.
Correct — unlabeled components cause interrupts and a never-updated stale diagram actively misleads; both are common mistakes.
Using arrows to connect components is normal practice, not a mistake — the mistake is leaving arrows unlabeled.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在图里塞入与 ML 判断无关的运维细节（K8s、负载均衡、分片）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-engineering is stuffing a diagram with ops detail (K8s, load balancers, sharding) irrelevant to ML judgment.

scenario: 面试评的是你的 ML 判断，你却在高层图里画满了 K8s pods、负载均衡器、数据库分片。
scenario_en: The interview assesses your ML judgment, yet you fill the high-level diagram with K8s pods, load balancers, and DB sharding.
q: 在图里画满 K8s、负载均衡、分片这些细节，会怎样？
q_en: What happens if you pack the diagram with K8s, load balancers, and sharding detail?
why: 这是过度工程：面试评的是 ML 判断不是 DevOps，画满基础设施细节既浪费时间又转移了焦点。除非面试官明确问，图应停在组件层（客户端、网关、feature store、模型服务、日志、监控）。
why_en: It is over-engineering: the interview scores ML judgment not DevOps, so stay at the component level unless asked.
options: 加分，展示你懂基础设施的方方面面
过度工程：面试评 ML 判断不是 DevOps，画满基础设施细节浪费时间又转移焦点
无所谓，画多画少都不影响评分
让图更完整，面试官会因此更信任你的设计
options_en: It adds points, showing you understand every facet of infrastructure.
Over-engineering: the interview scores ML judgment not DevOps, so packing in infra detail wastes time and shifts focus.
It does not matter; more or less detail has no effect on scoring.
It makes the diagram more complete, so the interviewer trusts your design more.
optionExplanations: 堆基础设施细节不加分——它转移了对 ML 判断的注意力，正是过度工程。
对；ML 面试评的是 ML 判断，除非被问，图停在组件层，别陷进 DevOps 细节。
并非无所谓——过度细节会吃时间、稀释 ML 信号，是明确的负面。
更多基础设施细节不等于更可信，反而暴露你没抓住这场面试评的重点。
optionExplanations_en: Piling infra detail does not add points; it diverts attention from ML judgment — exactly over-engineering.
Correct — an ML interview scores ML judgment, so unless asked, keep the diagram at component level and avoid DevOps detail.
It is not harmless — over-detail eats time and dilutes the ML signal, a clear negative.
More infra detail is not more credible; it reveals you missed what this interview assesses.

scenario: 设计演进了：你加了反馈回路和 feature store，但白板上的图还停在最初版本。
scenario_en: The design evolved: you added a feedback loop and feature store, but the whiteboard diagram is still the initial version.
q: 一张不随设计更新的旧图会造成什么？
q_en: What does a diagram that never updates with the design cause?
why: 从不更新的旧图会主动误导——它和你正在讲的设计不一致，面试官对着旧图理解会跑偏。修法是随设计演进补图：加上反馈回路、feature store、监控箭头，让图和口头保持同步。
why_en: A stale diagram actively misleads because it no longer matches the design you are describing, fixed by updating it as the design evolves.
options: 没影响，面试官会自动脑补最新版本
旧图主动误导——和当前设计不一致，面试官对着旧图理解会跑偏；应随演进补图
反而更好，保持图简洁不改动最省事
只在最后总结时才有问题，过程中不更新没关系
options_en: No effect; the interviewer mentally patches in the latest version.
A stale diagram actively misleads — it no longer matches the design and the interviewer's understanding drifts; update it as the design evolves.
It is actually better; keeping the diagram unchanged and simple is least effort.
It only matters at the final summary; not updating during the process is fine.
optionExplanations: 面试官不会脑补——他看到的是白板上的旧图，不一致就会误导。
对；旧图和当前设计脱节会主动误导，随演进加反馈回路/feature store 才保持同步。
保持不动省的是画图的力气，代价是图变成误导源，得不偿失。
过程中的不一致就已经在误导了，不是等到总结才出问题。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer does not mentally patch it; they see the stale board diagram, and the mismatch misleads.
Correct — a stale diagram diverges from the current design and misleads; update with feedback loop and feature store to stay in sync.
Keeping it static saves drawing effort but turns the diagram into a misleading source — a bad trade.
The mid-process mismatch already misleads; the problem is not deferred to the summary.

scenario: 面试后半段你已经画好带标注的高层图，现在要讲「feature store → serving → 网关 → 客户端」这条路径要在 50ms 内完成。
scenario_en: Later on, with a labeled high-level diagram drawn, you want to say the feature-store to serving to gateway to client path must finish within 50 ms.
q: 已经有标注好的图后，最有效的讲法是什么？
q_en: With a labeled diagram already drawn, what is the most efficient way to explain?
why: 指着图上的箭头说「这条路径要在 50ms 内完成」，而不是再口头复述整条路径。指认代替复述每次省 30-60 秒，累积能多换 1-2 分钟投到深度（影子部署、A/B 设计）。
why_en: Point at the arrows and say 'this path must complete under 50 ms' instead of re-narrating the whole path, saving 30-60 seconds each time.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官刚加入或明显没跟上，第一次仍要口头把路径讲一遍建立共识，之后再用指认代替复述。
options: 把整条路径从头到尾再口头复述一遍，确保讲清楚
指着图上的箭头说「这条路径要在 50ms 内完成」，用指认代替复述，每次省 30-60 秒
把图擦掉重画一张更详细的，再开始讲
在图旁边再写一大段文字说明这条路径
options_en: Re-narrate the entire path end to end verbally to be sure it is clear.
Point at the arrows and say 'this path must finish under 50 ms', substituting pointing for narration and saving 30-60 sec each time.
Erase the diagram, redraw a more detailed one, then start explaining.
Write a long paragraph beside the diagram describing this path.
optionExplanations: 再口头复述一遍浪费了图的价值——图存在的意义就是让你不用复述。
对；指认代替复述，每次省 30-60 秒，累积起来多出 1-2 分钟投到深度。
擦掉重画既费时又打断节奏，图已经够用就该用它指认。
在旁边写大段文字又回到冗长口头模式，违背了图的省时初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Re-narrating wastes the diagram's value; the diagram exists precisely so you need not narrate.
Correct — pointing substitutes for narration, saving 30-60 sec each time and compounding into 1-2 extra minutes for depth.
Erasing and redrawing costs time and breaks flow; if the diagram suffices, use it to point.
A long paragraph beside it returns to verbose narration, defeating the diagram's time-saving purpose.

scenario: 数据策略阶段你画数据流图，要把数据的完整生命周期串起来。
scenario_en: In data strategy you draw the data-flow diagram, chaining the full data lifecycle.
q: 把数据流图的环节排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the stages of the data-flow diagram correctly:
steps: 原始数据（日志、画像、上下文）
训练数据（经 join、聚合、特征抽取）
预测（模型对线上请求打分）
why: 数据流：原始数据→（转换）训练数据→预测→反馈回流重训。画的时候标清来源、转换、存储、批 vs 流、反馈回路——反馈回路正是体现你懂 training-serving skew 和持续学习的地方。
why_en: The data flow goes raw data, then transformed training data, then predictions, then the feedback loop back to retraining, with the loop showing continuous-learning awareness.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["原始数据
日志/画像"] -->|join/聚合| B["训练数据"] B --> M["模型"] M --> P["预测"] P -. 反馈 .-> A

scenario: 欺诈检测题进行到第 18 分钟，澄清和数据策略都只口头讲了、一张图没画，你正要开始模型设计。
scenario_en: At minute 18 on a fraud prompt, clarification and data strategy were verbal only with no diagrams, and you are about to start model design.
q: 此时最好的做法是什么？
q_en: What is the best move at this point?
why: 先暂停，补一张高层系统图把前面已讨论的组件锚定下来，再进入模型设计（架构非平凡的话配一张草图）。缺了高层图后面全靠口头会越来越乱；补图永远比继续裸讲强。
why_en: Pause and draw a high-level system diagram to anchor the components already discussed, then proceed to model design with a sketch if the architecture is non-trivial.
whenOtherWins: 若时间已所剩无几、马上要收尾，补一张详图可能来不及，此时用极简高层图或口头 recap 锚定即可。
options: 不管图了，直接开始模型设计，反正前面口头讲过了
先暂停补一张高层系统图锚定已讨论的组件，再进入模型设计（非平凡就配草图）
把前 18 分钟的内容全部推倒重来，从头再画
只画一张最详细的模型架构图，跳过高层图
options_en: Forget diagrams and start model design directly; you already covered it verbally.
Pause to draw a high-level system diagram anchoring the components already discussed, then proceed to model design (with a sketch if non-trivial).
Scrap the first 18 minutes and start over, redrawing from scratch.
Draw only the most detailed model-architecture diagram and skip the high-level one.
optionExplanations: 继续裸讲会让后面越来越乱，缺高层图这个共享锚点，讨论没有依托。
对；先补高层图把已讨论组件锚定，再进模型设计，必要时配草图，止损又不推倒重来。
推倒重来浪费已完成的 18 分钟，补一张图就够，不必从头再画。
跳过高层图直接画模型架构缺了共享锚点，高层图恰恰是永不跳过那张。
optionExplanations_en: Continuing verbally-only gets messier; without the high-level anchor the discussion has nothing to hang on.
Correct — draw the high-level diagram to anchor discussed components, then proceed to model design with a sketch if needed, stopping the loss without a restart.
Restarting wastes the 18 minutes done; one diagram suffices, no need to redraw from scratch.
Skipping the high-level diagram for a model-architecture one loses the shared anchor; the high-level is the never-skip one.

scenario: 三种图各自对应框架的一个阶段和一套标注。
scenario_en: Each of the three diagram types maps to a framework phase and a labeling set.
q: 填空：三种图各自的绘制时机。
q_en: Fill in: when each of the three diagram types is drawn.
text: 高层系统图在 {{澄清之后/min 5-8}} 画（永不跳过）；数据流图在 {{数据策略/min 8-15}} 画；模型架构草图在 {{模型设计/min 15-22}} 画，且仅当架构 {{非平凡}} 时。
text_en: The high-level system diagram is drawn {{after clarification, min 5-8}} (never skipped); the data-flow diagram during {{data strategy, min 8-15}}; the model-architecture sketch during {{model design, min 15-22}}, only when the architecture is {{non-trivial}}.
why: 三种图的时机映射到框架三个阶段：澄清后立高层图、数据策略画数据流、模型设计非平凡才画草图。记住时机才能在对的时刻用对的图。
why_en: The three diagrams map to three framework phases: high-level after clarification, data-flow in data strategy, and the sketch only for non-trivial architectures in model design.

scenario: 高层系统图和模型架构草图画的是完全不同粒度的东西。
scenario_en: The high-level system diagram and the model-architecture sketch depict entirely different granularities.
q: 高层系统图 vs 模型架构草图，在「粒度」上有什么区别？
q_en: High-level system diagram vs model-architecture sketch — how do they differ in granularity?
why: 高层系统图停在组件名+方向层级（客户端、网关、feature store、模型服务），画系统间关系；模型架构草图深入单个模型内部（输入特征、embedding 层、交互层、输出头）。一个是系统级，一个是模型内部级。
why_en: The high-level diagram stays at component-name-plus-direction level across the system, while the sketch goes inside one model's internal structure.
tradeoff: 高层系统图(组件间关系) vs 架构草图(单模型内部结构)
options: 两者粒度一样，只是画在白板不同位置
高层图停在组件名+方向（系统间关系），草图深入单模型内部（输入/embedding/交互/输出头）
高层图画模型内部，草图画系统组件，正好相反
高层图只用文字，草图只用图形，是表现形式的区别
options_en: Same granularity, just drawn in different spots on the whiteboard.
The high-level diagram stays at component-name-plus-direction (cross-system), while the sketch goes inside one model (inputs/embeddings/interaction/output heads).
The high-level diagram shows model internals and the sketch shows system components — exactly reversed.
The high-level diagram uses only text and the sketch only shapes — a difference in representation form.
optionExplanations: 两者粒度根本不同：一个系统级、一个模型内部级，不是画的位置问题。
对；高层停在组件+方向、画系统关系，草图钻进单模型内部结构，粒度截然不同。
方向反了：高层画系统组件、草图画模型内部，选项把两者对调了。
区别在粒度不在表现形式，两者都用框和箭头，不是文字 vs 图形。
optionExplanations_en: The two differ fundamentally in granularity: one system-level, one model-internal — not a positioning issue.
Correct — high-level stays at components-plus-direction for cross-system relations, while the sketch goes inside one model's structure, a sharp granularity difference.
Reversed: high-level shows system components and the sketch shows model internals; this option swaps them.
The difference is granularity, not representation form; both use boxes and arrows, not text vs shapes.

scenario: 你在高层系统图的 serving 箭头旁边有空间可以加一个注解。
scenario_en: You have room beside the serving arrow in the high-level diagram to add an annotation.
q: 在高层图上加什么样的量化注解最能体现系统思维？
q_en: What quantitative annotation on the high-level diagram best shows systems thinking?
why: 在关键处加量化注解：serving 箭头标 QPS/延迟、ETL 标批处理频率、草图标 embedding 维度。这些数字证明你在想扩展、延迟、漂移，而不只是把框连起来。
why_en: Add quantitative annotations where they matter, like QPS or latency on the serving arrow, to show you think about scaling, latency, and drift.
whenOtherWins: 若某处数字并不影响设计判断（如日志格式版本号），就别硬标，量化注解只加在扩展/延迟/漂移这类真正重要处。
options: 标上你最喜欢的框颜色代码
在 serving 箭头标 QPS/延迟——数字证明你在想扩展、延迟、漂移
标上这个组件是哪年发明的技术
把整段模型公式抄在箭头旁边
options_en: Annotate with your favorite color code for the boxes.
Put QPS/latency on the serving arrow — numbers show you think about scaling, latency, and drift.
Annotate which year the component's technology was invented.
Copy the full model formula beside the arrow.
optionExplanations: 颜色代码不携带任何工程信息，不体现系统思维。
对；QPS/延迟这类量化注解直接证明你在想扩展和延迟，是系统思维的信号。
技术发明年份是无关的历史事实，不影响任何设计判断。
抄整段公式是过度细节，图要停在组件层，量化注解是几个关键数字不是公式。
optionExplanations_en: A color code carries no engineering information and does not signal systems thinking.
Correct — QPS/latency annotations directly show scaling and latency awareness, the systems-thinking signal.
The invention year is an irrelevant historical fact that affects no design judgment.
Copying a full formula is over-detail; the diagram stays at component level, and annotations are a few key numbers, not formulas.

scenario: 数据流图上，一条转换路径是每日批处理，另一条是亚秒级流处理。
scenario_en: In the data-flow diagram, one transform path is daily batch and another is sub-second streaming.
q: 在数据流图上标注「批 vs 流」的延迟，主要传达什么信号？
q_en: Annotating 'batch vs streaming' latency on the data-flow diagram mainly signals what?
why: 标「batch, daily」「streaming, sub-second」直接体现你意识到 training-serving skew——如果训练用日更特征、线上用实时特征，两边不一致会掉点。延迟注解＝在展示你懂这个风险。
why_en: Labeling 'batch, daily' vs 'streaming, sub-second' signals awareness of training-serving skew, since mismatched feature freshness between training and serving degrades performance.
whenOtherWins: 若整条管线都是同一种时效（全批或全流），就不必特意对比标注，一句说明即可，避免冗余。
options: 传达你会用两种不同颜色的箭头
传达你意识到 training-serving skew——训练/线上特征时效不一致会掉点
传达这个系统很复杂，值得多给分
传达批处理一定比流处理更好
options_en: That you can use two different arrow colors.
That you are aware of training-serving skew — mismatched feature freshness between training and serving degrades performance.
That the system is complex and deserves more points.
That batch is always better than streaming.
optionExplanations: 颜色不携带工程含义，延迟注解传达的是对时效不一致的意识。
对；标批/流时效直接秀出你懂 training-serving skew 这个真实风险。
系统复杂度不是加分理由，注解传达的是具体的偏斜风险意识。
批不一定比流好，各有适用场景；注解不是在评优劣而是标时效。
optionExplanations_en: Colors carry no engineering meaning; the latency annotation conveys awareness of freshness mismatch.
Correct — labeling batch/streaming freshness shows you understand the real risk of training-serving skew.
System complexity is not a scoring reason; the annotation conveys concrete skew-risk awareness.
Batch is not always better than streaming; each fits cases, and the annotation marks freshness, not superiority.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏斜
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练和线上服务时特征时效或计算不一致，导致线上效果掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-serving skew is a mismatch in feature freshness or computation between training and serving, degrading online performance.

scenario: 你 5 分钟前已经口头讲清了某条流程，现在又想画一张图，但这张图只是把刚说的话重复一遍。
scenario_en: You verbally explained a flow 5 minutes ago and now want to draw a diagram that merely restates what you just said.
q: 如果一张图只是复述你 5 分钟前说过的话，该怎么办？
q_en: If a diagram just restates what you said 5 minutes ago, what should you do?
why: 这种图没有增量，画它是浪费时间。应该停下来，把这段时间重定向到面试官在意的某个取舍的深度上。图要么省时间、要么加清晰度，纯复述两者都不占。
why_en: A redundant diagram adds nothing, so stop and redirect that time to depth on a tradeoff the interviewer cares about.
options: 照画不误，多一张图总比少一张好
停下来，把这段时间重定向到面试官在意的某个取舍的深度上
把这张图画得更华丽，弥补它没有新信息
画完后再口头把内容第三次复述一遍
options_en: Draw it anyway; one more diagram is always better than one fewer.
Stop and redirect that time to depth on a tradeoff the interviewer cares about.
Make the diagram fancier to compensate for it having no new information.
After drawing it, verbally restate the content a third time.
optionExplanations: 多一张纯复述图不是「更好」——它不省时间也不加清晰度，纯浪费预算。
对；复述图没增量就该停，把时间投到面试官在意的取舍深度上更值。
华丽弥补不了没有新信息，画工不是内容，纯复述图本质没价值。
第三次复述只会更浪费时间，问题是内容重复不是次数不够。
optionExplanations_en: One more redundant diagram is not 'better'; it neither saves time nor adds clarity — pure budget waste.
Correct — a redundant diagram adds nothing, so stop and invest the time in tradeoff depth the interviewer cares about.
Fanciness cannot compensate for no new information; draftsmanship is not content, and a restating diagram has no value.
A third restatement wastes more time; the problem is repeated content, not too few repetitions.

scenario: 画图时如果迟疑、边画边纠结，会向面试官传递某种信号。
scenario_en: If you hesitate and second-guess while drawing, it sends the interviewer a certain signal.
q: 为什么要练到每种图都能在 90 秒内画完？
q_en: Why practice drawing each diagram type in under 90 seconds?
why: 画图时迟疑会传递「你对自己的设计没把握」的信号。练到三种图各能在 90 秒内画完，就能流畅落笔、不打断思路，也让面试官相信你对设计有信心。
why_en: Hesitation while drawing signals uncertainty about your own design, so practice each type to under 90 seconds for fluent, confident execution.
options: 为了比别的候选人画得更快，纯粹比拼速度
画图迟疑会传递「对自己设计没把握」的信号；练到 90 秒内能流畅落笔、显得有信心
为了在 90 秒内画完好省下时间玩手机
因为白板只租 90 秒，超时要收费
options_en: To draw faster than other candidates, a pure speed contest.
Hesitation while drawing signals uncertainty about your design; practicing to under 90 sec makes execution fluent and confident.
To finish within 90 sec so you can save time to check your phone.
Because the whiteboard is only rented for 90 sec and overtime is charged.
optionExplanations: 不是和别人比速度——是让自己流畅、不显迟疑，速度是手段不是目的。
对；迟疑＝没把握的信号，练熟到 90 秒内能流畅画完，既省时又传递信心。
省时间不是为了摸鱼，是为了把分钟投到取舍深度上。
白板收费是玩笑选项，和面试无关。
optionExplanations_en: It is not a speed contest with others; it is about fluent, hesitation-free execution — speed is a means, not the goal.
Correct — hesitation signals uncertainty, so drilling to under 90 sec makes drawing fluent and conveys confidence while saving time.
Saving time is not for slacking but for investing minutes in tradeoff depth.
Whiteboard rental fees are a joke option unrelated to the interview.

scenario: 你已画好带监控组件的高层图，面试官后续问「drift detection（漂移检测）怎么融进来？」
scenario_en: With a high-level diagram including a monitoring component drawn, the interviewer follows up 'how does drift detection fit in?'
q: 已有图作为共享参照时，怎么回答这个 follow-up 最高效？
q_en: With the diagram as a shared reference, how do you most efficiently answer this follow-up?
why: 指着图上的监控组件说「漂移检测在这里」，再补一条从监控回到数据/重训的箭头。图给了双方一个共享参照，让 follow-up 变成「在图上加一笔」而不是重新口头搭一遍上下文，对反馈回路尤其有效。
why_en: Point to the monitoring component and add an arrow from monitoring back to retraining, using the diagram as a shared reference so the follow-up becomes one stroke rather than rebuilding context verbally.
whenOtherWins: 若这个 follow-up 涉及一个图上完全没有的新子系统，可能需要在旁边另起一小块草图，而不是硬塞进现有图。
options: 从头口头重新搭一遍整个系统的上下文再回答
指着图上的监控组件说「漂移检测在这里」，补一条回到重训的箭头，把 follow-up 变成图上加一笔
说这个问题超纲了，图上没有就不回答
把整张图擦掉，专门为漂移检测重画一张
options_en: Rebuild the whole system's context verbally from scratch before answering.
Point to the monitoring component saying 'drift detection is here', add an arrow back to retraining, making the follow-up one stroke on the diagram.
Say the question is out of scope and refuse to answer since it is not on the diagram.
Erase the whole diagram and redraw one dedicated to drift detection.
optionExplanations: 重新口头搭上下文浪费了图作为共享参照的价值，图存在就是为了省这一步。
对；指认监控组件+补一条箭头，把 follow-up 变成图上加一笔，尤其适合反馈回路。
漂移检测正好挂在监控组件上，不超纲；拒答丢掉了轻松作答的机会。
擦掉重画既费时又丢了已建立的共享参照，补一条箭头就够。
optionExplanations_en: Rebuilding context verbally wastes the diagram's value as a shared reference — it exists to save exactly this step.
Correct — point to monitoring and add one arrow, turning the follow-up into a single stroke, especially apt for feedback loops.
Drift detection hangs right on the monitoring component, so it is in scope; refusing forfeits an easy answer.
Erasing and redrawing costs time and loses the established shared reference; one arrow suffices.

scenario: 画高层系统图时你在犹豫要画到多细：是画客户端/网关/feature store/模型服务这一层，还是继续往下画负载均衡、pod、分片。
scenario_en: Drawing the high-level diagram you weigh how deep to go: the client/gateway/feature-store/model-serving layer, or down into load balancers, pods, and shards.
q: 高层系统图默认该停在哪个粒度？
q_en: At what granularity should the high-level diagram stop by default?
why: 默认停在组件名+方向层级（客户端、API 网关、feature store、模型服务、日志、监控），除非面试官明确要求才往下画基础设施。因为面试评的是 ML 判断，往下画 pod/分片就是过度工程。
why_en: Stay at the component-name-plus-direction level (client, gateway, feature store, model serving, logging, monitoring) unless the interviewer asks to go deeper.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确追问基础设施细节（如「这个 serving 层怎么扩」），才往下画负载均衡/副本/分片，此时是被要求而非主动过度工程。
options: 画到最细，把负载均衡、pod、分片全画出来才算完整
停在组件名+方向层级（客户端/网关/feature store/模型服务），除非被要求才往下画
只画一个「系统」大框，内部什么都不画
画到芯片和网络协议级别，展示底层功底
options_en: Go to the finest detail — draw load balancers, pods, and shards for completeness.
Stop at component-name-plus-direction level (client/gateway/feature store/model serving), unless asked to go deeper.
Draw only one big 'system' box with nothing inside.
Go down to chip and network-protocol level to show low-level chops.
optionExplanations: 画满 pod/分片是过度工程，ML 面试评的不是 DevOps，除非被问不该往下画。
对；停在组件+方向层级，既表达清系统关系又不陷进无关的基础设施细节。
只画一个大框没有任何信息量，起不到锚定组件讨论的作用。
芯片/协议级别彻底跑偏，和 ML 系统设计的评估维度毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing pods/shards is over-engineering; an ML interview does not score DevOps, so do not go deeper unless asked.
Correct — stopping at component-plus-direction expresses system relations without sinking into irrelevant infra detail.
One big box carries no information and cannot anchor a component discussion.
Chip/protocol level is wholly off-track and unrelated to what ML system design assesses.

scenario: 你打算全程只用口头描述 YouTube 的「召回→排序→重排」多阶段流程，不画图。
scenario_en: You plan to describe YouTube's candidate-generation to ranking to re-ranking flow entirely verbally, no diagram.
q: 纯口头描述这种多阶段流程会有什么代价？
q_en: What is the cost of describing this multi-stage flow purely verbally?
why: 口头讲这种多阶段流程要花 2-3 分钟，且面试官容易在中途跟丢；一张图能让它瞬间清晰。代价就是时间和理解风险双输，正是该用高层图的场景。
why_en: Describing this multi-stage flow verbally costs 2-3 minutes and risks the interviewer losing the thread, whereas one diagram makes it instantly legible.
options: 没有代价，口头讲和画图效果完全一样
要花 2-3 分钟且面试官易跟丢——时间和理解双输，一张图能让它瞬间清晰
口头讲更好，因为不占白板空间
只有语速慢的人才有代价，语速快就没问题
options_en: No cost; verbal and diagram are exactly equivalent.
It costs 2-3 minutes and risks the interviewer losing the thread — losing both time and comprehension, while one diagram is instantly legible.
Verbal is better because it does not use whiteboard space.
Only slow speakers pay a cost; fast talkers have no problem.
optionExplanations: 并非等效——多阶段流程口头讲又慢又易跟丢，图能瞬间说清。
对；2-3 分钟＋跟丢风险是双输，多阶段流程正是该画高层图的典型场景。
省白板空间毫无价值，代价是时间和清晰度，口头讲不是更好。
语速快也难避免多阶段口头描述的跟丢风险，问题在结构不在语速。
optionExplanations_en: Not equivalent — a multi-stage flow described verbally is slow and easy to lose, while a diagram is instantly clear.
Correct — 2-3 minutes plus the lost-thread risk is a double loss, and a multi-stage flow is exactly when to draw a high-level diagram.
Saving whiteboard space is worthless; the cost is time and clarity, so verbal is not better.
Even fast talkers cannot avoid the lost-thread risk of verbal multi-stage description; the issue is structure, not speed.

scenario: 带标注的图让你用「指认」代替「复述」，每次省一点时间，累积起来可观。
scenario_en: A labeled diagram lets you point instead of re-narrate, saving a little each time that adds up.
q: 「指认代替复述」每次省多少、累积能换来什么？
q_en: How much does 'point instead of narrate' save each time, and what does it add up to?
why: 每次指认代替复述约省 30-60 秒，一场面试多次累积就多出 1-2 分钟，这些分钟正好投到深度（影子部署、A/B 设计）。反过来未标注箭头每次要 15-20 秒打断，是纯损耗。
why_en: Pointing instead of narrating saves 30-60 seconds each time, compounding to 1-2 extra minutes for depth, while an unlabeled arrow costs a 15-20 second interrupt each.
options: 每次省 5 秒，累积也就多几秒，可忽略不计
每次省 30-60 秒，累积多出 1-2 分钟投到深度；反之未标箭头每次要 15-20 秒打断
每次省半小时，一场面试能省出整整一步
省多少无所谓，画图纯粹是形式，不影响时间
options_en: Saves 5 sec each time, adding up to just a few seconds — negligible.
Saves 30-60 sec each time, compounding to 1-2 extra minutes for depth; conversely an unlabeled arrow costs a 15-20 sec interrupt each.
Saves half an hour each time, freeing a whole step in one interview.
The amount does not matter; diagramming is pure formality with no time effect.
optionExplanations: 不止省 5 秒——每次 30-60 秒，累积起来是能投到深度的 1-2 分钟。
对；指认每次省 30-60 秒累积 1-2 分钟，未标箭头每次 15-20 秒损耗，一正一反差距明显。
半小时是荒谬夸大，一场面试总共才 45 分钟。
省时间恰恰是画图的核心价值，说不影响时间是否定了本课的立论。
optionExplanations_en: Not just 5 sec — 30-60 sec each time compounds into 1-2 minutes you can invest in depth.
Correct — pointing saves 30-60 sec each, compounding to 1-2 min, while unlabeled arrows cost 15-20 sec each; the gap is clear.
Half an hour is absurd exaggeration; the whole interview is only 45 minutes.
Saving time is the core value of diagramming; claiming no time effect denies this lesson's thesis.

scenario: 题目刚给出、你还没澄清清楚范围，就想立刻上手画高层图。
scenario_en: The prompt just landed and, before clarifying scope, you want to start drawing the high-level diagram immediately.
q: 画高层图和问题澄清，谁先谁后？
q_en: Which comes first, drawing the high-level diagram or problem clarification?
why: 先澄清范围，再画图锚定实现讨论。范围没定清就画，容易画出一张针对错误问题的图，后面还得推倒。图是用来锚定「已经澄清的设计」，不是用来代替澄清。
why_en: Clarify scope first, then diagram to anchor the implementation discussion, because diagramming before scope is set risks anchoring the wrong problem.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官一上来就把范围、目标、约束都给死了，几乎无需澄清，那可以很快就进入画高层图的环节。
options: 先画图再澄清，让图引导你去问澄清问题
先澄清范围，再画高层图锚定实现讨论——范围没定就画容易画错问题
两件事同时做，边画边澄清最省时间
画图和澄清无关，随便哪个先都行
options_en: Draw first, then clarify, letting the diagram guide your clarifying questions.
Clarify scope first, then draw the high-level diagram to anchor the implementation discussion — drawing before scope risks the wrong problem.
Do both at once; drawing while clarifying saves the most time.
Diagramming and clarification are unrelated; either order is fine.
optionExplanations: 先画图会锚定一个还没定清的问题，画错了还得擦；澄清才是画图的前提。
对；澄清范围在前、画图锚定在后，避免为错误问题画图、后面推倒重来。
边画边澄清听起来高效，实则容易画到一半发现范围变了要重画。
两者有明确先后：澄清定问题、图锚定已澄清的设计，顺序不能随意。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing first anchors an unsettled problem and may need erasing; clarification is the prerequisite for diagramming.
Correct — clarify scope first then anchor with a diagram, avoiding diagramming the wrong problem and a later restart.
Drawing while clarifying sounds efficient but often means redrawing when scope shifts mid-way.
There is a clear order: clarification defines the problem and the diagram anchors the clarified design, so order is not arbitrary.
